_what: One row per user action: the regex for a call into its spine (`entry`), the files that own the spine, and the DOORS - every file outside the spine allowed to call it, each with the audit's verdict. Enforced by tests/templates/action-doors.test.ts on every jest run. Seeded 2026-11-18 from .rptc/research/entry-point-drift-audit/research.md (rows are its table's numbers).
_rules: A file that calls an entry and is not listed is a NEW DOOR and fails. Call an existing door instead, or add a row here with a reason a reviewer can read.
A listed door that no longer calls the entry is STALE and fails. Delete the row in the change that moved the call.
verdict `drift` or `lead` is an exemption: known debt, and it must name its fix in `fix`. Fixing the drift deletes or re-labels the row.

`modeRule` lists arguments the spine decides. A door passing one fails unless it carries `decidesMode`. On a drift door, `decidesMode` is debt and goes stale when the door stops passing the mode; on any other door it is a standing permission (the one entry point whose job IS that mode).
`mustRead` names spine result fields that hand the door a job. A door that does not read one fails unless it carries `doesNotRead`.
`bypasses` are files that do the action's job WITHOUT calling the entry. When one starts calling it, the row fails: move it to `doors`.
`agentOnlyHandlers`: a descriptor handler type no webview sends is a door only an agent reaches. Each needs a reason; one a webview now sends is stale.
`exemptionCeiling` counts drift and lead doors, bypasses and agent-only handlers. It only falls.
_notCovered: Rows 13 (start/stop demo: every caller runs the command), 18 and 19 (their doors are already pinned in spine-chokepoints.test.ts), and 24 to 30 (one handler type that the button and the agent descriptor both send). The audit's untraced list (edit project, export/import bundle, copy project, ERP actions, block-library promote/remove, added demos) is untraced here too.
